title: Advanced Single-Image Landscape Post-Processing in Photoshop (AK 3-1)

summary: This video presents an in-depth, single-image post-processing workflow for landscape photography, with a strong emphasis on crafting light, depth, and color in Photoshop rather than batch-processing multiple frames. The presenter walks through making the first image work by examining exposure, dynamic range, and foreground brightness, then demonstrates a multi-zone approach (sky, mountains, foreground) for targeted RAW adjustments, color grading, and light shaping. The tutorial showcases non-destructive editing via history-based layers, the use of an adaptive wide-angle modification and symmetry-focused cropping, and advanced tools and techniques (diffusion, level of blacks, dodge/burn for water and highlights, clone-paint for blending exposures, selective color for color separation, and edge refinement). Throughout, the emphasis is on leading the viewer’s eye toward light, preserving natural color, and saving multiple versions to revisit decisions, all illustrated against ice-cave and sunset scenes in Alaska.

sections.title: Workflow basics, first-image selection, and initial exposure planning
sections.description: Sets up the 'post-processing system' premise, explains processing the first image rather than scanning a batch, and introduces the rationale for half-stop bracketing and ETTR-oriented thinking.

sections.title: Dynamic range, ISO considerations, and foreground exposure
sections.description: Discusses how ISO affects dynamic range (doubling ISO reduces range by about 1/3 stop), pricing foreground brightness, and the logic of keeping ISO low while preparing to reveal foreground detail.

sections.title: Initial edits: RAW whites, color temperature, and zoning
sections.description: Shows replacing exposure with a whites-focused RAW adjustment, balancing color temperature, applying a wide-angle transformation for composition, and cropping to achieve symmetry.

sections.title: Ice cave processing: three-zone approach and directional lighting
sections.description: Details a three-zone approach for ice-cave scenes (and notes a four-zone mindset when relevant), emphasizes creating directional light from the left, expands shadows, uses diffusion to imply distance, and refines edges to maintain natural transitions.

sections.title: Non-destructive edits and advanced texture work
concepts: selective color vs HSL for color separation
sections.description: Demonstrates maintaining a fully non-destructive workflow via history-based edits, employing clone-paint to blend exposures, refining edges, and using diffusion-style texture to enhance depth and atmosphere while discussing color-separation tactics.

sections.title: Wrap-up and future topics
sections.description: Concludes with notes on saving multiple versions, preserving history, and previewing upcoming topics such as drone footage and additional black-and-white processing.
